==English==

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:bor|frm:machine|tree=1}}
{{bor+|en|frm|machine}}, from {{der|en|la|māchina||a machine, engine, contrivance, device, stratagem, trick}}, from {{der|en|grc-dor|μᾱχᾰνᾱ́}}, cognate with {{cog|grc-att|μηχᾰνή||a machine, engine, contrivance, device}}, from which comes {{m|en|mechanical}}.  Displaced native {{noncog|ang|searu}}.

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|Q11019}}A device that directs and controls [[energy]], often in the form of [[movement]] or [[electricity]], to produce a certain effect.
#* {{RQ:Economist|title=A better waterworks|date=2013-06-01| volume=407| issue=8838| page=5 (Technology Quarterly)| url=http://www.economist.com/news/technology-quarterly/21578526-medical-technology-artificial-kidneys-are-getting-closer-becoming-clinical| passage=An artificial kidney these days still means a refrigerator-sized dialysis '''machine'''. Such devices mimic the way real kidneys cleanse blood and eject impurities and surplus water as urine.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625180618/http://www.economist.com:80/news/technology-quarterly/21578526-medical-technology-artificial-kidneys-are-getting-closer-becoming-clinical|archivedate=25 June 2017}}
# {{lb|en|dated}} A vehicle operated mechanically, such as an [[automobile]] or an [[airplane]].
#* {{RQ:Burroughs Return of Tarzan|version=Burt|pages=40–41|pageref=41|passage=As he stood directly beneath a brilliant arc light, waiting for a limousine that was approaching to pass him, he heard his name called in a sweet feminine voice. Looking up, he met the smiling eyes of Olga de Coude as she leaned forward upon the back seat of the '''machine'''. He bowed very low in response to her friendly greeting. When he straightened up the '''machine''' had borne her away.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|author=F. Britten Austin|title=The Air-Scout|journal=The Strand Magazine| location=London| publisher=George Newnes, Ltd.| month=July|year=1914| volume=XLVIII| page=568| pageurl=https://archive.org/stream/TheStrandMagazineAnIllustratedMonthly/TheStrandMagazine1914bVol.XlviiiJul-dec#page/n581/mode/2up| passage=As the aviator turned his '''machine''' to reconnoitre in the new direction, he was surprised to see the hostile aeroplane between him and his objective.}}
# {{lb|en|telephony|abbreviation}} An [[answering machine]] or, by extension, [[voice mail]].
#: {{ux|en|I called you earlier, but all I got was the '''machine'''.}}
# {{lb|en|computing}} A [[computer]].
#: {{ux|en|Game developers assume they're pushing the limits of the '''machine'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|He refuses to turn off his Linux '''machine'''.}}
# {{lb|en|figuratively}} A person or organisation that seemingly acts like a machine, being particularly [[efficient]], [[single-minded]], or [[unemotional]].
#: {{ux|en|Bruce Campbell was a "demon-killing '''machine'''" because he made quick work of killing demons.}}
#: {{ux|en|The government has become a money-making '''machine'''.}}
# Especially, the group that controls a political or similar organization; a combination of persons acting together for a common purpose, with the agencies which they use.
#* {{RQ:Landor Imaginary Conversations|III|Rousseau and Malesherbes|passage=The whole '''machine''' of government, civil and religious, ought never to bear upon the people with a weight so oppressive}}
# {{lb|en|poetry}} Supernatural agency in a poem, or a superhuman being introduced to perform some exploit.
#* {{RQ:Spectator|author=Addison||351|April 21 1712|passage=I am apt to think, that the changing of the Trojan fleet into water-nymphs, which is the most violent '''machine''' in the whole Æneid{{...}}}}
# {{lb|en|politics|chiefly|US}} The system of [[special interest group]]s that supports a political party, especially in urban areas.
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1902|journal=The Friend
|passage=A '''machine''' politician cannot see why the straight ticket (as he and his clique of party bosses prepare it) should not be voted by every citizen belonging to that party.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2006|author=Jerry F. Hough|title=Changing Party Coalitions: The Mystery of the Red State-blue State Alignment|publisher=Algora Publishing|isbn=9780875864082|page=37
|passage=In essence, therefore, the right-fork strategy of the Democrats meant an alliance of the South with the political '''machines''' built on the non-Protestant immigrants in key Northeastern states.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2013|author=Paul M. Green; Melvin G. Holli|title=The Mayors: The Chicago Political Tradition, fourth edition|publisher=SIU Press|isbn=9780809331994|page=126
|passage=He was thrust into a political maelstrom for which he was ill-prepared, and yet he was, most notably, the Chicago '''machine''''s political savior.}}
# {{lb|en|euphemistic|obsolete}} [[penis|Penis]].
#* {{RQ:Cleland Fanny Hill|1|107|He now reſumes his attempts in more form: firſt he put one of the pillows under me, to give the blank of his aim a more favourable elevation, and another under my head, in eaſe of it: then ſpreading my thighs, and placing himſelf ſtanding between them, made them reſt upon his hips: applying then the point of his '''machine''' to the ſlit, into which he ſought entrance;}}
# {{lb|en|historical}} A contrivance in the Ancient Greek theatre for indicating a change of scene, by means of which a god might cross the stage or deliver a divine message; the [[deus ex machina]].
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} A [[bathing machine]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1823|author=w:Frances Burney|title=Journals and Letters|page=512|publisher=Penguin|year_published=2001
|passage=One '''Machine''' only was provided for Bathers, the Limitted smoothness of the sands not extending widely enough to admit another.}}
